title: Are teenagers really so selfish?
situation: An English-language magazine you regularly read has published an article claiming that young people today do not care about their community. You disagree with some of its points. Write a letter to the editor in response to the article.
situationHu: Egy angol nyelvű magazin cikke szerint a mai fiatalok nem törődnek a közösségükkel; írj olvasói levelet a szerkesztőnek.
stimulus:
"Today's teenagers only care about their phones and themselves. They never help their neighbours, they don't volunteer and they show no interest in the community they live in."
(from the article 'A Generation Without Community Spirit')

points.text: say why you are writing and react to the claim made in the article
give examples of how young people in your area help others
explain what might stop teenagers from getting more involved in their community
suggest how schools or local communities could encourage young people to help more

checklistExtra: A levél elején egyértelmű, melyik cikkre és milyen állításra reagálok?
Minden érvemet példával vagy indoklással támasztottam alá?

modelAnswer.text:
Dear Editor,

I am writing in response to the article 'A Generation Without Community Spirit', published in your last issue. While I agree that many teenagers spend too much time on their phones, I strongly disagree with the claim that we show no interest in our community. It is unfair to generalise about a whole generation.

In my town, Kecskemét, young people help others in many ways. For instance, many students at my school volunteer at the local animal shelter at weekends, and last winter our class collected food and warm clothes for homeless people. Some of my friends also do the shopping for elderly neighbours who cannot leave their homes.

Admittedly, not every teenager is involved, but this is partly due to the fact that we have very little free time. With long school days, private lessons and exam preparation, it is difficult to commit to regular voluntary work. Many young people also simply do not know where help is needed.

One possible solution would be for schools to work more closely with local charities and organise volunteering days. Local councils could also set up a website listing short, flexible volunteering projects. Above all, young people should be given more opportunities to take responsibility and have their ideas heard.

In conclusion, today's teenagers are not selfish; they simply need more support and encouragement.

Yours faithfully,
Zsófia Kiss
